Fit a first-capture-conditional CJS model

Source: R/cjs.R
drm_cjs.Rd

Fit a first-capture-conditional CJS model

Usage

drm_cjs(
  data,
  phi = ~1,
  p = ~1,
  phi_data = NULL,
  p_data = NULL,
  selection = NULL,
  sd_phi = NULL,
  sd_p = NULL,
  terminal_constraint = NULL,
  control = list(),
  contrasts = list(phi = NULL, p = NULL),
  engine = c("tmb", "julia")
)

Arguments

data

A cmr_data object.

phi

Survival formula, with logit unit-time apparent survival. M3 accepts at most one shared random intercept, such as (1 | site).

p

Detection formula, with logit detection conditional on alive. M3 accepts at most one shared random intercept, such as (1 | site).

phi_data

Optional interval predictor table keyed by id, interval_start, and interval_end.

p_data

Optional detection predictor table keyed by id and occasion.

selection

Optional list(eligibility = occasion_indices, assumption = "alive_available"). Conditions each individual's likelihood on first capture at the realized occasion under an alive-and-available reference cohort. Shared-effect selection is unsupported.

sd_phi, sd_p

Optional one-sided formulas for log SD of the persistent individual survival or detection effect. Predictors must be constant within individual.

terminal_constraint

Optional named list fixing exactly one common final-process probability, for example list(phi = 0.8) (unit-time survival) or list(p = 0.4) (final-occasion detection). Values must be strictly between zero and one. It applies at the final declared interval or occasion, not at each individual's administrative endpoint.

control

Options passed to stats::nlminb().

contrasts

Optional named list of process-specific contrast specifications, list(phi = ..., p = ...). The fitted coding is retained for prediction and bootstrap refits.

engine

Computational engine: native TMB or native CJSModels.jl. The Julia bridge currently admits fixed-effects CJS only.

Value

A drm_cjs fit containing the optimizer and TMB objective. Individual-effect fits also report quadrature refinement status and an order_timings table with setup/optimization time, optimizer status, iterations, and function and gradient evaluation counts. These timings describe the fit that ran; they do not establish parameter recovery or inference calibration.

Examples

y <- rbind(c(1,0,0), c(1,0,1), c(1,1,0), c(1,1,1))
d <- cmr_data(y, frequency = c(20, 10, 10, 10))
fit <- drm_cjs(d)
coef(fit)
